title: Canonical module pullback reads normalized stratum trivializations
statement: Let f:X→S, i:X′→X and j:S′→S be scheme morphisms, and Λ a finite commutative ring. Let F be a constant-coefficient module sheaf on the vanishing site V_f [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Suppose its normalized restriction along (i,j), as defined by identity-base-change normalization followed by stratumRestriction [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf], is finite type locally constant [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf]. Let r be a constant-module geometric morphism [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison] from the oriented triple site for (f∘i,j) [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology] to V_f, whose set inverse image is naturally isomorphic to sheafified left Kan extension along the canonical triple functor (U,V,W)↦(U×_X X′,V,W×_S S′), with the associativity comparison for i,f and unchanged second structural arrow. Then the fixed-ring module sheaf underlying r*F admits a covering sieve of the terminal triple, and on each member its slice is isomorphic to the constant sheaf with some finite Λ-module value. Scalar restriction is the canonical CommRingCat-to-RingCat comparison followed by [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]. This is a statement about one pair of maps, with no assertion that stratifications exist and no nearby-cycle or Psi-goodness hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the assumed finite-type local-constancy witness on this one normalized stratum. Normalize the second structural arrow using the isomorphism between base change along the identity of S and the identity functor. No stratification is constructed in this lemma.

Compose normalization with stratum base change. Base-change associativity on the first outer entry and the identity-pullback projection on the second identify the resulting triple functor with the concrete functor specifying r. Each comparison respects the three generating cover types. The set inverse images are the corresponding sheafified left Kan extensions, so uniqueness of left adjoints gives their natural isomorphism.

Apply the constant-ring module equivalence to this inverse-image comparison. The scalar actions agree on constant sections, and extension along the sheafification unit is unique. Thus the fixed-ring sheaf of r*F agrees with the fixed-ring sheaf of the normalized stratum restriction. This concerns the actual canonical module pullback, not an arbitrarily chosen functor on modules.

Evaluate the local-constancy witness at the terminal triple. Scalar restriction commutes with restriction to its slices and identifies the constant module models with constant fixed-ring module sheaves. Compose the slice isomorphisms with the comparison above. Keep the covering sieve and finite-type module models; finite generation over the finite coefficient ring makes their underlying sets finite. The argument also applies to empty strata and the zero ring.

theorem canonical_stratum_trivializations {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (i : X' ⟶ X) (j : S' ⟶ S)
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (r : Morphism (vanishingDatum.{u, u + 1} f)
        (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j))
    (hr : Nonempty (r.inverse ≅
        sheafToPresheaf (vanishingTopology.{u, u + 1} f) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
          (Comma.map
            ((Functor.rightUnitor ((etaleBaseChange i).prod (etaleBaseChange j)) ≪≫
              (Functor.leftUnitor ((etaleBaseChange i).prod (etaleBaseChange j))).symm).hom)
            (show (etaleBaseChange.{u, u + 1} f).prod' (𝟭 (EtaleSite S)) ⋙
                (etaleBaseChange i).prod (etaleBaseChange j) ⟶
              𝟭 (EtaleSite S) ⋙
                (etaleBaseChange (i ≫ f)).prod' (etaleBaseChange j) from
              { app := fun V ↦ ((etaleBaseChangeComp i f).inv.app V, 𝟙 _)
                naturality := fun V W h ↦
                  Prod.ext ((etaleBaseChangeComp i f).inv.naturality h) (by simp) })).op.lan ⋙
          presheafToSheaf (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).topology
            (Type (u + 1))))
    (F : (vanishingDatum.{u, u + 1} f).modules (Coeff.{u, u + 1} Λ))
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant
      (productTopology (i ≫ f) (j ≫ 𝟙 S)) (Coeff Λ)
      ((stratumRestriction f (𝟙 S) i j Λ).obj ((vanishingModuleTransport f Λ).obj F))) :
    letI : HasFiniteLimits (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).objects :=
      OrientedPointCohomology.triples_finiteLimits (i ≫ f) j
    ∃ R : (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).topology.Cover
      (⊤_ (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).objects),
    ∀ (Z : (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).objects)
      (k : Z ⟶ ⊤_ (OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).objects), R k →
      ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Coeff.{u, u + 1} Λ), Finite M ∧
        Nonempty
          (((constantRingModuleRestriction _ (Coeff Λ)).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (realizationRingIso _ (Coeff Λ)).inv).obj
              ((r.modulePull (Coeff Λ)).obj F))).over Z ≅
            (constantSheaf
              ((OrientedPointCohomology.datum.{u, u} (i ≫ f) j).topology.over Z)
              (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Coeff.{u, u + 1} Λ))).obj M)
